Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 W.P.No.34445 of 2023
O R D E R:

Heard learned counsel for petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Roads & Buildings appearing for respondent Nos.1 & 4, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent No.2 & 3, and perused the record.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is that they are the inam land holders; that 1st petitioner is having land to an extent of Ac.0.08 gts in survey Nos.930 & 931 and petitioner Nos.2 to 5 are the having land to an extent of Ac 0-7 gts., each, in all totaling to Ac.0.38 gts, in survey No.739,
situated at Velmagudem Village, Peddavoora Mandal, Nalgonda District; and that the respondents had acquired the aforesaid land for the purpose of widening of R & B road from Musalamma Chettu to Gurrampode via petitioners' village viz., Velmagudem, without passing any award and without paying any compensation, which action it is contended as arbitrary, illegal and contrary to the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'Act 30 of 2013').
3. Counter affidavit on behalf of respondent No.1 & 4, and counter affidavit on behalf of respondent No.3 are filed, separately.
4.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
By the counter affidavit filed on behalf of respondent Nos.1 & 4, sworn on 11.11.2024, it is stated that the said respondents are pursuing the matter by addressing letters to other respondents and had sent requisition letter, dt.18.02.2024, to the District Collector, in respect of the subject lands and in reply, the 2nd respondent had addressed letter, dt.16.03.2024, calling upon the said respondent to submit required forms and documents for initiating land acquisition proceedings;
and that respondent Nos.1 & 4 have sent revised proposal to the 3rd respondent on 11.11.2024,
requisitioning for acquiring the lands of the petitioners, in all, admeasuring Ac.0.38 gts in survey No.739, 930 & 931 situated at Velmagudem Village, Peddavoora Mandal, Nalgonda District.
5.
Learned Government Pleader appearing for respondent Nos.1 & 4 thus submits that the said respondents have already initiated action by submitting the requisition proposal to the 3rd respondent.

sentences.text:
The 3rd respondent, by the counter affidavit filed and sworn on 09.12.2024, claims that the lands to an extent of Ac.0-38 gts in survey Nos.739, 930 & 931 situated at Velmagudem Village,
Peddavoora Mandal, Nalgonda District, is covered in laying of R & B road from Musalamma Chettu to Gurrampode; and that during the land acquisition proceedings initiated earlier, as the petitioners did not file Occupancy Right Certificate (ORC), the said lands were not acquired and the petitioners were not paid compensation.

7. By the counter affidavit it is further stated that though the 3rd respondent had received requisition for acquiring the aforesaid lands from the 4th respondent, since, as per the provisions of the Act, conducting a Socio Economic Survey is mandatory, the 3rd respondent had requested the 4th respondent to obtain necessary exemption in Form-A from the Government; and that on the 4th respondent furnishing the aforesaid exemption, the 3rd respondent would proceed with the acquisition of lands of the petitioners and also pay compensation in terms of the provisions of the Act 30 of 2013.
8.
I have taken note of the respective submissions made.

9. The respondents, by their separate counter affidavits filed, do not dispute the fact of the lands of the petitioners being affected by the road widening/alignment, for which the authorities are required to acquire the lands of the petitioners.

10. Though the 4th respondent, by the counter affidavit filed by him, had claimed the authorities having initiated correspondence with other departments for acquiring the lands, the fact of the 4th respondent sending a request to the 3rd respondent for acquiring the lands on 11.11.2024 i.e., on the same day as the counter affidavit in the present Writ Petition is filed by the said respondent into the Court, only goes to show that the said respondent did not initiate action earlier and only to save himself from this Court examining the matter in detail, has claimed of the authorities having initiated proceedings for acquiring the lands of the petitioners.

11. Further, the 3rd respondent having informed the 4th respondent of the necessity to obtain exemption from conduct of Socio Economic Survey, for the said authority to initiate land acquisition proceedings, would also go to show that the 4th respondent authority only as mere eyewash has made the said statement of the said authority having initiated proceedings for acquiring the lands of the petitioners, though an Award for acquiring the other extents of lands was passed in the year 2000, thereby depriving the petitioners of the fruits of their land for 23 long years i.e., up to the date of filing of the Writ Petition.

Even, now the requisition sent by the 3rd respondent on 11.11.2024 being an incomplete requisition, without obtaining necessary exemption from government for conduct of Socio Economic Survey, would further goes to show that the said requisition is a defective requisition, which cannot be acted upon by the 3rd respondent for initiating proceedings for acquiring the lands of the petitioners.

12. The said conduct on the part of respondents No.1 & 4 in not initiating land acquisition proceedings even though a road, affecting the land of the petitioners, was laid in the year 2000,
thereby depriving the petitioners of their property.

The said action on part of the respondents would Andugula Chinna Eedaiah vs The State Of Telangana on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27563833/
2 amount to the authorities depriving the petitioners of their constitutional right to property under Article 300A of the Constitution of India.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
13. However, as the respondents-authorities now claim to have initiated land acquisition proceedings, though being defective, this Court is of the view that the respondents-authorities are to be directed to complete the entire process of acquiring the lands of the petitioners to an extent of Ac.0-38 gts in survey Nos.739, 930 & 931 situated at Velmagudem Village, Peddavoora Mandal,
Nalgonda District, as per the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and complete the entire exercise,
including payment of compensation to the petitioners, within a period of six (06) months from today.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 14. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed.
No order as to costs.
15. Consequently, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in these writ petitions shall stand closed.
T. VINOD KUMAR, J 12th December, 2024.
